newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria releases list of plane crash victims.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria releases list of plane crash victims.

text.p: Nigeria on Sunday finally released the list of 142 people killed last Thursday when a Boeing 727 operated by a local airline crashed without any survivors.
The flight manifest released in the capital Abuja by Aviation Minister Air Commodore Ita Udo-Imeh showed at least 30 foreigners, including prominent Costa Rican lawyer Joacquin Tacsan.
Diplomats said other foreigners included British, Indian, Italian, American, French and Israeli nationals.

The casualties included Nigerian social science professor Claude Ake, who resigned last year from a commission appointed by oil giant Shell to study the ecology of the oil-producing Niger Delta in protest at the execution of minority rights activist Ken Saro-Wiwa.
The plane operated by Aviation Development Company (ADC) crashed into a lagoon in a mangrove jungle 40 kms (25 miles) northeast of Lagos on Thursday and was not found until the following day.
The plane was coming from the oil city of Port-Harcourt and some of the foreigners may have been executives of oil companies.
Initially ADC said there were 141 people on board including crew members but later put the figure at 143. The manifest released by the minister contained 142 names.
No one has explained the discrepancy.

Salvage teams at the crash scene had not yet found the aircraft's "black box" recorder containing communication between the pilot and the ground, aviation sources said. They said finding it was crucial to determining the cause of the accident.
The crash was the worst in Nigeria since September 1992 when a C-130 transport plane went down in swamps near Lagos killing 173 mostly senior military officers.
